scenario: AITA for wanting to let my family know my daughter is getting married and post one or two pictures of the cake I'm baking on social media? | My daughter is getting married to her boyfriend of 2 years at the courthouse next week, while he's on leave from the army. This is not a shotgun wedding. They do not plan to have kids for the foreseeable future (if ever.) They intend to have a proper wedding in the future, when finances allow. However, in the meantime, she's forbidden me from mentioning it to anyone in our family or even friends of mine who know her, but do not know the family. These are kids who never had an apartment and want us (the parents) to give them what they need to get started. It's a financial imposition to ask us to furnish their house, and I know that both my family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they could. In addition, the groom's family all knows this is going to happen and I feel our family will be terribly hurt if they are shut out completely. We're not inviting people to the courthouse, obviously, but they can call and offer their Congratulations anyway. I'm worried that, when they finally do have their wedding, nobody will want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Further, I make lots of crafts and baked goods. I like to post the projects on social media for critiques and she's forbidden me from posting the wedding cake picture. Her real wedding will have a professional cake, but I wanted the practice, around just a few of us will be there. Frankly, my enthusiasm for helping her is dwindling and I am contemplating *not* baking the cake, as literally this exposure was all I wanted. I'm also thinking of offering her less for setting up house. My original thinking was, they could save up faster if they don't have to buy furniture and dishes. But she won't let us enlist the help of others. We have to replace what we give her and do without in the meantime, because we don't have money to buy these things right now. We're willing to do this for their comfort. It sure would be nice to see if anyone else is planning on getting rid of some old furniture or dishes so they can get started. Am I being an asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me break it down step by step. First, my daughter is getting married, and she's been with her boyfriend for two years. They're planning a courthouse wedding because he's on leave from the army. They don't plan to have kids for a while and want a proper wedding when they can afford it. So far, this seems like a normal situation. But here's the thing: she's forbidden me from telling anyone in the family or even my friends who know her but not the family. That's a bit confusing. Why wouldn't she want to share this news with our family? I mean, I understand that sometimes people want privacy, but completely shutting out the family feels extreme, especially since they're planning a proper wedding later. She also doesn't want me to post pictures of the cake I'm baking on social media. I make a lot of crafts and baked goods, and I usually share them for feedback. This cake is just for practice since only a few of us will be there. She's against me posting it, which is making me less enthusiastic about helping her. I'm even considering not baking the cake at all because this exposure was all I wanted. Additionally, she doesn't want us to ask others for help setting up their house. We were planning to give them furniture and dishes to save them money, but she's against it. We have to replace what we give them, which is a financial burden. I'm thinking maybe we can ask others if they have things to get rid of, but she's not into that either. I'm worried that if we don't tell the family now, they'll feel hurt later, especially when they finally have the proper wedding. They might not want to come if they feel they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Plus, I feel like our family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they knew. So, am I being an asshole? I don't think so. I just want to share the news with our family, post a picture of the cake I'm making, and help my daughter and her husband get started without financial strain. It seems like her restrictions are causing more problems than they're solving. I'm trying to be supportive, but her lack of communication and willingness to accept help is making it hard. I guess I'm feeling like she's not considering our feelings and the potential hurt that could come from excluding the family. I want to do the right thing, but I'm not sure how to handle her wishes without causing more issues down the line.
